name: ManipulationNet
ability_definition: The ability to quickly move your hand, your hand together with your arm, or your two hands to grasp, manipulate, or assemble objects.

task_realism.reasoning: Peg-in-hole insertion with clearances down to 0.02 mm, cable routing, and grasping from clutter are canonical industrial assembly and handling tasks. They closely mirror real work such as fitting parts, routing wire harnesses, and bin-picking. They are still abstracted task-board versions of that work, not full products or multi-step assembly sequences with varied part geometries.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: It runs on real hardware with physically manufactured NIST kits, a fixed reproducible protocol, completion-time measurement, and audited results. That is far closer to real work than simulation. However, lab setups are controlled, part presentation is known in advance, and there is no sustained throughput, fatigue, or production-line variability. The Human-in-the-Loop protocol, where a human reports task status, also adds a slightly artificial scaffold.

construct_coverage.reasoning: It spans grasping, manipulation, precise assembly, and speed, which together match the definition's key components better than most alternatives. The task set is still small: five peg shapes, cable management, and clutter grasping. It has no aggregate score, and the reported result covers only peg-in-hole. Bimanual coordination, tool use, and diverse object types are thinly represented.

format_match.reasoning: Inputs are real physical objects and outputs are real physical outcomes: an inserted part, a routed cable, a grasped item. Success and completion time are graded like workplace output. The standardized task-board artifacts, rather than genuine manufactured products, make the format somewhat stylized.

transferability_reasoning: ManipulationNet tests real robots on real, precision-manufactured assembly and handling tasks with success and speed metrics, which aligns well with the grasp-manipulate-assemble definition of Manual Dexterity. Transfer is limited by the narrow, standardized task set and controlled lab conditions. The reported score also covers only the peg-in-hole slice, not the full range of workplace dexterity demands.

2026.model_or_system: InsertAnything (RL insertion policy trained only in simulation, using fingertip force feedback)
2026.metric: percent of the 20 ManipulationNet peg-in-hole tasks completed (5 hole shapes × 4 clearance levels); reported as 20/20
2026.human_reference: General adult / manual assembly workforce (typical assembler or technician doing hand insertion and fitting of parts)
